figures.description: Woodcut line diagram for the ratios 4:3, 3:2 and 2:1: three pairs of parallel horizontal lines, with capital letters at the ends and at the division ticks and small numerals under some segments. Pair 1: upper line A-B (A at left, B at the right end-stroke), divided by three ticks labelled above C, a letter shaped like a reversed D (probably D), and E; the numeral 4 stands under the segment E-B. Lower line from a second reversed-D-shaped letter at the left to F, which stands directly under E; it has ticks under C and under the first reversed D, labelled below I and K. Pair 2: upper line L-N (end-stroke before N), divided by two ticks labelled above P and Y (Y preceded by a stray capital B, printed 'BY'); the numeral 3 stands under the segment Y-N. Lower line M-o (M at left with end-stroke, small o after the right end-stroke under Y), with one tick under P labelled below R; the numeral 2 stands below this line between R and o, immediately above the Z of pair 3. Pair 3: upper line S-V (end-strokes at both ends) with one tick in the middle labelled Z above; the numeral 2 under the segment Z-V. Lower line T-X ending under Z, with the numeral 1 under it. The pairs show 4 parts against 3, 3 against 2 and 2 against 1 (sesquitertius, sesquialter, duplex).

reading_text.text: pariter consonante, ut octavo cum primo, undecimo cum quarto, duodecimo cum quinto, quintodecimo cum octavo, gravibus nimirum una cum acutis, aut acutis cum gravibus peraequa proportione simul ascendentibus vel descendentibus, in intensionibus remissionibusve.
Porro tonus et hemitonium et diesis per se ipsa considerata, principium quidem consonantiae sunt, sed nondum tamen consonantia.

Conficitur autem Dia-tessaron duobus tonis et hemitonio et modica praeterea toni parte, quae diesi minor, nomine vacat: Dia-pente vero tribus tonis et hemitonio: et Dia-pason sex tonis: ac Dia-pason cum Dia-tessaron, tonis octo et hemitonio: Dia-pason cum Dia-pente, novem tonis et hemitonio: bis Dia-pason tonis duodecim.

Ratio autem intervalli Dia-tessaron, est sesquitertia: Dia-pente, sesquialtera: Dia-pason, duplex: Dia-pason cum Dia-tessaron duplex-superpartiens: Dia-pason cum Dia-pente, triplex: Bis Dia-pason, quadruplex: ut exempli gratia in numeris, primus proponatur nobis terminus, numerus sex, cuius sesquitertius est plane octo: sesquialter, novem: duplex, duodecim: duplex-superpartiens, sedecim, sex bis continens, et duas eius partes: triplex, octodecim: quadruplex, viginti quatuor.

Verumtamen sciendum, rationes intervallorum, non ex sonorum, aut ex chordarum numero iudicari; sed ex intentione vocis a gravi ad acutius: quandoquidem intervallum Dia-pente, cuius est ratio sesquialtera, sesquialterum minime videtur ex ratione numeri sonorum, quo numero superat sonos, qui ipsum praecedunt. Nam primi soni quincuplex invenitur: secundi vero, duplum sesquialterum: tertii, superpartiens: quarti, sesquiquartum: nullius vero sesquialterum demonstrari potest. Ab intensione itaque acuti, non a sonorum numero, sesquialterum censetur. Idem autem et in reliquis quoque rationibus nobis licebit considerare.

Inventae autem hae sunt intervallorum rationes et deprehensae, ex dispari chordarum vel longitudine vel crassitudine: vel ea, quae per torsionem claviculorum fit, intensione; aut, quod compertum magis, ex ponderum e nervis appensione: In iis vero quae inflata sonant, aut ex fistularum amplitudine, aut ex intensione spiritus ac remissione.

Systematum autem hoc quidem Tetrachordum est, quod omnes intervalli Dia-tessaron continet facultates: aliud vero Pentachordum, quod intervalli Dia-pente facultates complectitur: aliud Octachordum, quod totam intervalli Dia-pason vim continet: aliud deinceps Heckaedecachordum, bis Dia-pason universam comprehendens intensionem, duplicesque habens facultates: eas enim, quas modo diximus, atque intervallorum Dia-pason Dia-tessaron, et Dia-pason Dia-pente, et bis Dia-pason facultates in se continet.
Differunt autem Systemata ab intervallis quae in ipsis sunt, quod illa in materia consistunt: intervalla vero a materia abstracta consideramus.

Harmoniae porro proprium est Systemata illa componere aptareque ad aliquod genus modulationis, ut ad Diatonon, ad Chromaticon, et ad id quod ab ipsa harmonia cognominatum, Harmonicum dicimus. Si igitur tonis plurimum harmonia peragitur, Diatonon sic vocatum efficitur genus: si Hemitoniis, Chromaticum: si vero diesibus fere harmonia continetur, conficitur, quam Harmonicam appellant modulationem.

Verumenimvero neque omnino tonis, quae ad Harmoniam pertinent, efferuntur, neque hemitoniis omnino, neque omnino diesibus: hoc enim fieri non potest: quinimo, quoniam ex tribus intervallis Dia-tessaron intervallum confectum est, duobusque tonis et hemitonio comprehensum, necesse est, postquam duo prima intervalla imposueris, reliquum esse Hemitonium: atque hoc fuerit Dia-tessaron Diatonon cognominatum genus, ex Hemitonio et tonis constans duobus. Si vero duo sint hemitonia, reliquum fuerit unum ex confusione intervallum, Trihemitonium simplex: eritque id Dia-tessaron genus Chromaticum, ex Hemitoniis duobus et Trihemitonio temperatum, quod priore moestius luctuosiusque est. Si vero per duas dieses modulatio peragatur, quod reliquum est intervallum, erit unum ditonium ex confusione, ac Dia-tessaron hoc genus Harmonicum nominatur, quod sit optimum, ab ipsa communi omnium harmonia cognominatum.

Eodem modo et caetera quoque systemata constituit harmonia, temperatque. Ex proposito enim exemplo, quo ostensum in uno tetrachordo, quomodo intervalla intervalli Dia-tessaron constituantur, facile studiosus alia systemata quomodo componantur, assequi poterit.

Genus autem Harmonicum est modulatu difficillimum, meditatione multa exercitationeque indigens: unde eius est usus rarior. Diatonum vero est simplum et generosum et magis naturale: quare id et Plato admittit.

Horum autem unumquodque rursus variatur, et in multas divisiones et differentias et genera modulationum distribuitur: et modo Lydius, modo Phrygius, modo Dorius appellatur modulus: a quorum quolibet Paeon, Hymenaeus, Exodius, et quotquot sunt modulationum genera, existunt. Non enim sola intervallorum mutatione, neque sola eorum differentia: sed etiam lentioribus, et concitatis transitionibus, pausis quoque et fluxibus, atque variis tactibus pulsibusque, pro vario manus temperamento, infinitae et diversae modulationes conficiuntur.

doubts: Chapter number III for the paragraphs on pp. 48-50 is inferred: the print gives only the paragraph numbers 8-12, and the next heading is 'CAP. 4.' (50.12). The first line of p. 48 continues the paragraph numbered 7 on p. 47 (not seen), hence 'III.7 (continued)'.
No printed marginal notes on pp. 48-53; the only marginal print is Vinet's paragraph numbers (not counted as lines).
48.3: the punctuation between 'octauo' and 'graui-' is a faint small mark; read as a comma.
48.21 'iuterualli': at high enlargement the second letter is open at the top like u, not a damaged n; treated as a turned n (misprint).
48.23: the second 'Dià pason' has no hyphen, no circumflex and an apparently undotted i; corrected in the reading text to 'Dia-pason' (typographic only).
49.20 'censetur': the n is blotted and resembles a barred u; read as n.
50.1 'quoque': the second o is damaged (ring with a central dot); the reading is certain.
50.5 'datum': the letter after 'da' is t-shaped with a small hook at the top; it could be a damaged r. Either way the sense needs 'chordarum' (listed as a misprint).
50.21 'Heckædecachordum' (Heckaedecachordum in the reading text) kept as printed; the spelling with ck is odd but not certainly a misprint.
51.2-3: a thin curved brownish line over 'pénte,' and 'continet' looks like a hair or fibre on the page rather than a reader's mark; recorded only in the line notes.
51.23: the first letter of the second 'neque' is weakly inked and could be read u ('ueque', perhaps a turned n); transcribed 'ṇeque' with the uncertainty dot. The reading text has 'neque'.
51.24: a stray mark above the d of 'diesibus' is not an accent; not transcribed.
Catchword at the foot of p. 51 is 'test,' (comma); the first word of p. 52 is 'test:' (colon). The text follows p. 52.

Figure on p. 49: two labels have the form of a reversed D (left end of the lower line of pair 1 and above the middle tick of its upper line); a stray capital B stands before the label Y in pair 2. Described as printed.

Reddish thin strokes on pp. 48, 50, 52 and 53 may be a reader's red crayon marks or fibres; the dash after 'fue' (52.9) clearly supplies the missing hyphen and is the most likely to be a reader's addition.
49.15 'quincuplex' and the other numbers are transcribed as printed; the content was not checked against any other text (Latin-only task).
Reading text: spacing around punctuation normalised (no space before , ; : .); the hyphen of the compounds Dia-tessaron, Dia-pente, Dia-pason and duplex-superpartiens kept as printed.
